questions.question: Why is the OpenTelemetry instrumentation file loaded with node --import before the application?
options: Because instrumentation patches modules such as node:http and pg as they load, so it must start first
Because --import makes the app run faster
Because the SDK only works in CommonJS
questions.explanation: Auto-instrumentation works by patching modules when they are loaded, so the SDK has to start before any application code imports them.

questions.question: What is the role of the W3C traceparent header?
options: It carries the trace ID, parent span ID and sampling flag across a network hop
questions.explanation: traceparent propagates trace context between services, so spans in different services join one trace.

questions.question: Why should userId not be used as a metric attribute?
options: It creates one time series per user (high cardinality) and can overwhelm the metrics backend
OpenTelemetry forbids attribute names that contain Id
questions.explanation: Metric attributes should be low-cardinality; per-user values explode the number of series.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of tail sampling over head sampling?
options: It decides before the request starts, so it is cheaper
It removes the need for metrics
It can keep all error and slow traces because the decision is made after the trace is complete
questions.explanation: Tail sampling buffers complete traces in the Collector, so it can keep errors and slow requests; head sampling might drop the one trace you needed.
